use: The battle's signal station (the field object 'signal') on its cell in every state, in the eastern battles; the objective's marker shows whether it is secured.

generator.prompt: A Roman signal post on the eastern frontier: a stout square pillar of pale sun-dried mudbrick on a low stone plinth, about two point six metres tall and eighty centimetres square, its flat top carrying an iron fire basket, a palm-trunk pole lashed to one side flying a long red woollen signal banner, a short palm-trunk ladder leaning against it, and beside it a heap of dry brushwood and palm fronds for the beacon fire; about one and a half metres across at its foot. Pale mudbrick, grey stone, palm wood, black iron, dry brushwood and red wool. Single isolated static prop for a grounded painterly-realistic historical game set in the third century Roman world. Physically based aged materials, believable hand-made construction and a bold, solid, readable silhouette from above, restrained surface detail, level base and complete geometry from every side. No environment, ground plane, decorative display plinth, modern materials, text, logos or people.

review.scope: Tripo's own render, four views of the final compressed model with a 1.8 m figure for scale (scripts/assets/preview-model.mjs), and the battles in the desktop build at High
review.notes: A pillar of pale dressed stone, not the mudbrick asked for, on a paved stone plinth, with a fire basket and a bundle of brushwood on its top, a ladder, and a pole flying a small red pennant rather than a long banner. Accepted: it reads as a post of its own beside the Roman mast. Processed at 2.8 m: 1.85 by 2.21 m on the ground.
